notes: Check batch: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. result.json gives head e83b4f2 with uncommitted changes (not 9fde8f6 as the brief says); the skill copy the runs read (scratchpad/check4/skill) is identical to the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, which differs from e83b4f2 only by the new do: rule in SKILL.md.

git diff db91c23 -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches only SKILL.md (the one-step with rule, the new do: rule, the captures rule) and testing.md (Assert with patterns). macros.md and library-design.md are unchanged, so the seven rules graded in the previous sweep are graded to the same standard as <previous>/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json: a direct attribute write inside get's quote counts against Keep quote blocks small, validation in the macro body outside quote does not; a one-line three-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them.

Judgement call under Keep `quote` blocks small: haiku-1's get quote (lines 46-51) records the route with Module.put_attribute(__MODULE__, :tiny_router_routes, ...) rather than @tiny_router_routes. It is the same direct write into the caller's attribute that the previous standard counted as a violation, and it does not call a TinyRouter function, so it is graded violated. No earlier run had this exact shape.

New rule, graded against its text in idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md (Readability): Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else. Violating runs out of four, per sentence. "Use `do:` for a body of one expression that reads as part of the head: an accessor, a predicate, or a short pattern-matching clause.": 0 of 4 (no do: on a body of more than one expression). "A body with several steps, a `case` or `with`, or a comment gets `do ... end`.": 0 of 4. "When one clause of a function needs a block, keep the short clauses on `do:` and set the block clause apart with a blank line; when several clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks.": blank-line part 0 of 4 (haiku-2 validate_path!/2 and sonnet-2 validate_path!/1 do it right); several-blocks part 3 of 4 (haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2, each in a four-clause match_segments/3 with two do: clauses and two block clauses). "A one-liner that `mix format` has to wrap onto a `do:` line of its own is a body that wants a block or a helper.": 3 of 4 (haiku-1 bind/3 twice; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 validate_handler!/1, both from the long guard when is_atom(handler) and handler not in [nil, true, false]). Any sentence: 4 of 4. The match_segments/3 block clauses are one-expression bodies that would wrap under do:, so the fourth sentence sends them to blocks and the third then requires the two do: clauses to become blocks too.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace in scratch Mix projects (one per run, the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex, so xref line numbers match the run file, with real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex). haiku-1 and haiku-2 expand the handler with Macro.expand and xref reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile). sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use Macro.expand_literals with function {:match, 1} set in the env and xref reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime).

Bad-declaration checks: each run's file loaded, then one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and another declaring get "/", "not a module" compiled with Code.compile_string. All eight fail while the router compiles: haiku-1 and haiku-2 with CompileError raised while get expands; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 with ArgumentError from __define__/3, which get's quote calls. Messages omit the nofile:3: location prefix.

Format: all four pass mix format --check-formatted (each run wrote get("/", MyApp.PageHandler) with parentheses in the example router, so the locals_without_parens caveat of the previous sweep does not arise) and compile without warnings with elixir and with mix compile.

Reads: all four read SKILL.md, macros.md and library-design.md before writing the file, matching result.json reads and satisfying the Expected reads line. haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 used Read calls and read each reference twice; haiku-1 read SKILL.md and both references through cat in Bash calls, then library-design.md again with Read.

Against the previous sweep: haiku still makes handlers compile-time dependencies in both runs (now both through Macro.expand), and both haiku runs moved from recording through a function to writing the attribute in get's quote; both sonnet runs now record through __define__/3 and stay runtime-only. The spec rule stays clean in all four.

Smoke test outside the rules: all four return routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", and return :error for "/nope"; sonnet-1 returns string param keys (%{"id" => "42"}), the others atom keys (%{id: "42"}).
